name: Chargify
tagline: The B2B SaaS subscription and usage billing engine formerly sold as Chargify. It is now available only as Maxio Advanced Billing.
shortDescription: Chargify started in 2009 as a subscription billing platform. It merged with SaaSOptics in 2021 and took the Maxio name in 2022, and the engine now ships as Maxio Advanced Billing. Entry price is the Maxio Grow plan at $599 per month.
longDescription:
Chargify is now sold as Maxio Advanced Billing, and there is no way to buy it under the Chargify name. Type chargify.com into a browser and you get a 301 redirect to maxio.com/chargify, a landing page headed "Chargify is now Maxio". The word Chargify appears nowhere on Maxio's current price list. The software itself is in good health. What disappeared was the brand. Chargify began in 2009 as the billing engine behind the telephony company Grasshopper, built by David Hauser and Siamak Taghaddos, and spun out on its own after Mark Cuban invested in 2011. Scaleworks bought it in June 2016 and ran it from San Antonio, Texas. Battery Ventures then put more than $150 million into Chargify and SaaSOptics in April 2021, and the merged company announced the Maxio name in April 2022. Traces of the old brand still sit in the plumbing: API sites resolve on chargify.com subdomains, hosted signup pages run on chargifypay.com, the help centre lives at maxio-chargify.zendesk.com, and the usage billing object in the REST API is still called Chargify EBB. Those are legacy hostnames, not evidence that the brand is still for sale.

Pricing and how it works

There is no Chargify rate card, because there is no Chargify SKU. Buyers land on Maxio's two published bands instead. Grow costs $599 per month for companies billing up to $100,000 a month; Scale is a custom quote above that threshold. Seats are unlimited and annual billing is the default. Optional modules, among them advanced revenue management, A/R management and multi-entity support, each carry their own line item, so a finance team's real invoice usually clears the sticker price by a wide margin. None of that money buys card processing. Advanced Billing pushes charges out to one of 22 connected gateways, and the percentage you pay per transaction is set by that gateway or its acquirer.

Who it is for

The Chargify engine was built for B2B SaaS companies whose pricing refuses to stay simple: tiered components, quantity-based add-ons, metered usage, proration and stacked coupons. That is still its strongest suit. Anyone arriving from a search for Chargify pricing is really shopping for Maxio, so the comparison set that matters is Chargebee, Recurly, Zuora and Stripe Billing rather than any card processor.

What Chargify is not

Chargify never was a card acquirer and never issued merchant accounts. It sits above the payment layer, storing gateway tokens rather than raw card numbers, and connects to Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, Authorize.Net, Square, GoCardless, Worldpay, PayPal, Elavon, Cybersource and a dozen more. If a consultant or reseller quotes you for Chargify today, ask which Maxio plan and which optional modules that number covers, because the two are not the same purchase.

faqs.question: Is Chargify still available?
faqs.answer: Not under that name. Chargify merged with SaaSOptics in 2021 and the combined company rebranded as Maxio in April 2022. The billing engine is still sold and still developed, but it ships as Maxio Advanced Billing. Visiting chargify.com now returns a permanent redirect to a Maxio page, and Maxio's own pricing page does not mention Chargify anywhere. Existing customers keep their accounts and API sites still resolve on chargify.com subdomains, but there is no Chargify product, contract or price list to buy today.

faqs.question: How much does Chargify cost?
faqs.answer: You pay Maxio's prices. Grow is $599 per month for companies billing up to $100,000 monthly, and Scale is a custom quote above that threshold. User seats are unlimited on both and annual billing is the default. Optional modules such as advanced revenue management, A/R management and multi-entity support are charged separately. None of those figures include card processing: charges are routed to a gateway you connect, so the per-transaction rate comes from that gateway or its acquiring bank.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Chargify and Maxio?
faqs.answer: Chargify is the older half of Maxio. Battery Ventures invested more than $150 million across Chargify and SaaSOptics in April 2021, and the two were folded into one company that took the Maxio name a year later. Chargify contributed the subscription and usage billing engine, now called Advanced Billing. SaaSOptics contributed revenue recognition and SaaS metrics reporting. So Chargify is a component of Maxio rather than a competitor to it, which is why comparison pages that pit one against the other are comparing a product to its own parent.

faqs.question: Is Chargify a payment processor?
faqs.answer: No, and it never was. Chargify was a billing layer that sat above your payment stack, and Maxio Advanced Billing works the same way. It manages plans, invoices, proration, dunning and usage metering, then hands the actual charge to a gateway you already have. Maxio lists 22 connected gateways including Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, Authorize.Net, Square, GoCardless, Worldpay, Elavon and PayPal. You still need a merchant account. The percentage plus fixed fee on each transaction is set by that gateway, not by the billing platform.

faqs.question: What are the best Chargify alternatives?
faqs.answer: Chargebee, Recurly, Zuora and Stripe Billing are the usual shortlist for B2B SaaS companies that would once have bought Chargify. Chargebee and Recurly are the closest like-for-like swaps on subscription mechanics and dunning. Zuora goes further into enterprise quote-to-cash and prices accordingly. Stripe Billing is the cheapest route if you already process on Stripe and can live inside one vendor. Compare on revenue recognition support, gateway independence and the cost of optional modules, because headline plan prices rarely survive contact with the final invoice.
